gitCommit.subject: fix(api): one error chokepoint — stop leaking Postgres driver text to callers (hiez, 2eoy, 13ya, ibl) (#320)
gitCommit.body:
fix(api): one error chokepoint — stop leaking Postgres driver text to callers (hiez, 2eoy, 13ya, ibl) (#320)

The 500 fallback in errorResponse() echoed error.message, so any unmapped error
returned raw driver text (relation names, constraint names, sometimes column
values) to the caller — including an UNAUTHENTICATED caller via
GET /api/shared-results/[token]. 13 more routes hand-rolled their own catch and
did the same. The docblock documented the leak as intended and a passing unit
test pinned it, so code, comment and test all agreed — and all agreed wrongly.

- errorResponse() is now the sole error path: no response body is ever derived
  from a caught error. Unmapped -> { error: generic, errorId } (crypto.randomUUID).
- The full error goes to ONE structured log line, [api_error], keyed by the same
  errorId: name/message/stack (read explicitly — they're non-enumerable, so
  JSON.stringify(error) is "{}"), the recursively-unwrapped cause chain (drizzle
  wraps the driver error), and the postgres-js snake_case driver fields.
  query/parameters are omitted — they carry user values.
- Detail is inlined in the body ONLY when NODE_ENV !== "production". Deliberately
  NOT VERCEL_ENV: Vercel sets NODE_ENV=production on PREVIEW deploys, and preview
  URLs are shareable. Pinned by a test that stubs production and asserts the body
  is exactly { error, errorId }.
- Curated/typed domain errors are unchanged — they stay the sanctioned channel
  for user-facing copy and specific statuses. A test catches over-generalization.
- ESLint no-restricted-syntax makes it hold for the NEXT route: no reading
  .message under src/app/api. Watched failing on a reintroduced leak; it catches
  the (error as Error).message cast form too.

Also closes three gaps found while in here:
- purses-2eoy's "enum backstop gap" was live, not latent: the authz-enumeration
  gate's regex couldn't see `export const { GET, POST } = toNextJsHandler(auth)`,
  so the ENTIRE better-auth surface was invisible to the filesystem-exhaustive
  authz test and its two PUBLIC_OR_SELF keys were dead. A zero-method backstop
  now fails loudly naming any route that yields no methods.
- purses-13ya: Header's display-name fallback no longer derives from the email
  local-part.
- purses-ibl: dead listInvitations() (return [] behind a stale TODO) deleted.
- purses-fh3e: bcryptjs + @types/bcryptjs removed (dead since better-auth).

Gates: lint 0 errors, test:ci 1295 passed, test:db 652 passed, build, auth:verify.
